answer: Attention Ledger Escrow.** Each identity must pre-commit a fixed block of verifiable sustained attention — measured as continuous low-latency response to random challenges — before it can transact. The ledger records a rolling sonnet-length sequence of those responses. Miss a window and the escrowed attention is forfeited, leaving a hollow record that blocks re-entry. Enforcement runs across a mesa of concurrent identities: each one pays the full attention cost independently, so scaling sybils multiplies real human-hours linearly rather than amortizing them.
